name: Question 5
problem:
$$
A=[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & 0 \\ -2 & 6 & 0 \\ 3 & -6 & 2\end{aligned}]
$$

Consider the matrix $A$ shown above. What are the dimensions of the eigenspaces ${V}_{2}$ and ${V}_{5}$ corresponding to eigenvalues $\lambda =2$ and $\lambda =5$ of $A$, respectively?
worked_solution:
First, we write down the characteristic equation $\text{det}(A-\lambda I)=0:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{det}(A-\lambda I)=0 \\ |\begin{aligned}1-\lambda  & 2 & 0 \\ -2 & 6-\lambda  & 0 \\ 3 & -6 & 2-\lambda \end{aligned}|=0 \\ (2-\lambda )|\begin{aligned}1-\lambda  & 2 \\ -2 & 6-\lambda \end{aligned}|=0 \\ (2-\lambda )((1-\lambda )(6-\lambda )+4)=0 \\ (2-\lambda )({\lambda }^{2}-7\lambda +10)=0 \\ (2-\lambda )(\lambda -2)(\lambda -5)=0 \\ (\lambda -2)^{2}(\lambda -5)=0.\end{aligned}
$$

Hence, ${\lambda }_{1}={\lambda }_{2}=2$ (double root) and ${\lambda }_{3}=5$ (simple root).

Let's now consider the eigenspaces corresponding to each eigenvector:

- First, we consider $\lambda =5.$ Since ${V}_{5}$ corresponds to a simple root, we obtain 

$$
\text{dim}({V}_{5})=1.
$$

- Then, we consider $\lambda =2,$ which is a repeated root of the characteristic equation. To find the dimension of ${V}_{2},$ we row-reduce the matrix $(A-2I)\text{x}=0:$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}A-\lambda I & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & 0 \\ -2 & 6 & 0 \\ 3 & -6 & 2\end{aligned}]-2[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-1 & 2 & 0 \\ -2 & 4 & 0 \\ 3 & -6 & 0\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{2}:={R}_{2}-2{R}_{1} \\ {R}_{3}:={R}_{3}+3{R}_{1}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}-1 & 2 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

In the reduced matrix above, there is one pivot column (the $1$st one). This implies that we will have $3-1=2$ linearly independent eigenvectors corresponding to the eigenvalue $\lambda =2.$ Therefore, 

$$
\text{dim}({V}_{2})=2.
$$

dim(V2)=2 and dim(V5)=2
